messages:
sam_sales: Kicking off POC with Nimbus Financial — they want streaming chat with function/tool-calls + strict structured JSON output for downstream ETL. Running in their VPC (private) but want hosted fallback. Need alignment on SDKs, auth (ephemeral creds), and pricing (Dedicated vs hosted).
jordan_se: Great. Any technical checklist from their side? Are they using Go server + Rust workers, or something else? Also need SAML SSO details + IP egress whitelist.
sam_sales: They prefer Go for the API layer and Rust for heavy preprocessing. Key asks: ephemeral creds, per-route quotas, external KMS/HSM, audit logs, DPA, and latency SLO ~200ms p50.
aisha_eng: For streaming + function-calls, here's a minimal Go handshake snippet you can share: ```go
client := redwood.NewClient("$TOKEN")
stream, _ := client.StreamChat(ctx, opts)
stream.Send(ChatMessage{Role:\"user\", Content:prompt})
for msg := range stream.Recv() { fmt.Println(msg.Text) }
``` Use `function_call:{"name":"lookup_account","arguments":{...}}` to trigger tool-calls.
jordan_se: For structured output we recommend explicit schema + function-calls. Example JSON Schema (validated on our side): {"type":"object","properties":{"account_id":{"type":"string"},"balance":{"type":"number"}},"required":["account_id"]} — we can fail-fast if response doesn't match.
priya_security: Security flags: if there's any PHI we require Private/on-prem deployment. We need their SOC2 docs, network diagram, and allowed IPs. KMS: we support AWS KMS/GCP CMEK for Private; HSM via partner. Please have them sign the DPA; may need a DPIA depending on data class.
sam_sales: Procurement also wants delta pricing: hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved GPU cost, plus on-prem SOW/installation fees. They asked for an SSO flow diagram and how token rotation works.
trent_finance: Ballpark numbers to start: hosted (in examples) ~ $0.02 / 1k tokens for standard models (we'll provide an up-to-date sheet). Dedicated reserved capacity begins at ~$8k/month per GPU node for baseline commits (exact depends on config). I'll attach formal pricing spreadsheet after review.
aisha_eng: Recommendations for performance/cost: dynamic batching up to 16 for throughput, int8 quantization for cost-sensitive variants, prefix/KV caching for common prompts. For canary rollouts we can route 5% traffic to new model variant and auto-fallback on error.
jordan_se: POC runbook (high level): 1) creds & network peering setup 2) sample Go/Rust quickstart 3) functional tests (tool calls + schema checks) 4) load test (qps/latency) 5) security review 6) procurement / SOW sign 7) gradual production cutover. Who will own each step?
sam_sales: I'll handle sales + procurement coordination. Jordan + Aisha will own dev onboarding and quickstarts. Priya will lead security review. Trent will handle invoicing/pricing.
deploybot: Note: created POC workspace `nimbus-poc-1950`. Ephemeral creds set to 24h by default; request longer TTL via ticket.
priya_security: Add to checklist: token rotation every 24h (recommend), readonly audit trail, and confirm log retention — default 30 days, extendable on enterprise contract. Also require HMAC-signed callbacks for any webhook invocations.
aisha_eng: Quick question: do they want the model to call internal services (webhook enrichment) or only produce structured JSON which their ETL will call?
sam_sales: Both. Primary flow: model calls internal `account-lookup` webhook for enrichment, then returns a structured payload to ETL. They want proof that we can sign callbacks and retry on failures.
jordan_se: For webhook callbacks: if their firewall disallows inbound, we can proxy callbacks via a signed outbound connector or use an outbound polling pattern. We sign callbacks with HMAC and include replay-protection nonce.
sam_sales: Customer asked for demo latency numbers on Dedicated (8k context) — can we share p50/p95 on A10G?
aisha_eng: Rough numbers: p50 ~120ms, p95 ~400ms on A10G for optimized runtime (depends on batch size & model variant). Mark these as estimates; precise numbers from benchmark run will follow.
trent_finance: Action items: send pricing sheet + SOW + runbook + security checklist by EOD tomorrow. Sam/Jordan can you draft?
sam_sales: Yep, will draft pricing & SOW. Jordan will assemble quickstart repos for Go + Rust.
jordan_se: On it — I'll spin up a quickstart repo with streaming+function-call examples and schema validation tests, and drop links here when ready.
sam_sales: Thanks all :thumbsup: if anyone sees blockers call out now; otherwise I'll start drafting the docs and cc finance/security.
